issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement's UML and the solution implement addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch is structural: tests and expected usage assume a single-argument method. Students following the problem description or the solution will find the template's signature incompatible and may be unable to compile or run tests that expect addGuestStudents(int).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is desired, implement it inside that single-parameter method or provide an overloaded private helper method; do not require a boolean parameter in the public API so it matches the UML and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies addGuestStudents(int) but the template Lecture.java declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). The solution implements addGuestStudents(int). The extra boolean parameter in the template creates a mismatch between the exercise requirement and the starter code, causing confusion about the required method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (or, if the boolean was intentional, update the problem statement and solution to document and implement the validateInput parameter).
